title: Some Examples and Counterexamples in Oka Theory
summary: This paper gives examples and counterexamples in Oka theory: two about deleting closed sets from complex Euclidean space, one about blowing up along a connected Oka center, and one about deforming continuous maps to regular maps. Two positive results show that $\mathbb{C}^3\setminus S$ is Oka for every closed set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, and that the complement of the closed Hartogs triangle in $\mathbb{C}^2$ is Oka.
